subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: RSA Encryption
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on RSA Encryption.

hook.text: Three MIT researchers turned a math problem into the encryption that protects almost everything online.

buildup.text: RSA relies on one fact: multiplying two huge prime numbers is easy, but reversing the result is nearly impossible.

discovery.text: Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman published RSA in 1977. It became the foundation of internet security.

twist.text: RSA keys must grow larger as computers get faster. What was secure in 1977 is breakable now.

climax.text: RSA turned a mathematical curiosity into the lock on every secure website, email, and transaction.

punchline.text: Multiply two primes. Nearly impossible to reverse.

quiz.question: What mathematical principle makes RSA encryption secure?
options: Multiplying large primes is easy but factoring the result is extremely hard
Random number generation that never repeats
The speed of light limits how fast keys can be tried
